display.purpose: Auth headlines only, hard-wrapped like a prompt. Responsive 24-44sp.

body.purpose: Default working text, data, and short prose. The one body size (14sp).

label.purpose: Uppercased buttons, key names, eyebrows (12sp Bold).

micro.purpose: Stat captions (11sp), pills (10sp), nav labels (9sp). Uppercased.

textTiers.name: primary
textTiers.purpose: Headlines, titles, values, the thing being read.

textTiers.name: faint
textTiers.purpose: Disabled content, decorative meta, placeholders, inert chevrons.

motion.name: state

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: The single ambient animation; held static under reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: Debbie looks like a precision tool, not an app. A multimeter, a label printer, a terminal: one job, a fixed typeface, no opinion about delighting you. Everything is monospace, everything is square-cornered, and surfaces are flat sheets of warm paper separated by hairline rules rather than shadow. There is exactly one loud color, used for warnings, focus, and the current selection, never decoration. Hierarchy is built from weight and four opacity tiers first, size second. This is a deliberate rejection of generic Material 3, torrent-site UI, consumer streaming apps, and SaaS dashboards.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface, JetBrains Mono, for everything including prose.
Zero corner radius on every container, button, field, and control; pills and the progress bar are the only rounded shapes.
Flat by default: depth comes from 1px hairlines and warm tonal layering, never shadow.
A single Signal-orange accent, rationed to one element per screen.
Warm neutral palette (ink on paper) with a true dark inverse.
Hierarchy from weight and opacity tiers (100/72/60/40%) first, size second.
Strict 4dp spacing grid, with 6dp the single named exception.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal appears on at most a single conscious element per screen: a focused field, the active progress bar, the current selection, or an error. It is never decorative.

rules.name: The Labeled Status Rule
rules.body: Sap, Amber, and Signal never communicate alone. Every status hue is bound to an uppercased text label.

rules.name: The One Font Rule
rules.body: Everything is JetBrains Mono. No prose exception, no display face, no system-sans fallback. Differentiate by weight, opacity tier, or size, not family.

rules.name: The Four-Tier Rule
rules.body: All text and iconography is Ink at one of exactly four opacities: 100, 72, 60, 40%. Snap to these; do not invent intermediate alphas.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Label Rule
rules.body: Every micro-label (button, pill, stat caption, nav label, key name) is uppercased to signal 'machine readout.'

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. To make a surface distinct, lift its tone (Paper to Bone) or outline it with a 1px Faint border.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn at exactly 1px Faint, never thicker, never a colored stripe. Only opacity varies: 72% structure, 55% in-card divider.

dos: Do set everything in JetBrains Mono. No exceptions, no second family.
Do build hierarchy from weight and the four opacity tiers (100/72/60/40%) first, size second.
Do keep every container, button, field, and control at 0dp radius; reserve 999dp for pills and the progress bar.
Do pull every spacing value from the 4dp grid (4/8/12/16/20/24/32), with 6dp the single named exception.
Do draw structure as 1px Faint hairlines at 72% or 55%; selection thickens to Ink, focus is a 2dp Signal ring.
Do give every clickable a pressed tint (Ink 8%), a focus ring, and a 48dp touch target.
Do ration Signal to one element per screen.
Do derive status color and label from the state table; pair every hue with an uppercased label.
Do write copy that states facts; assume the user knows the domain.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface, a system-sans fallback, rounded cards, tonal shadows, dynamic-color purple, or FABs.
Don't ship stock Material Switch or Checkbox; use DebbieToggle and DebbieCheckbox.
Don't rely on Material's round ripple on square surfaces; use the flat pressed tint.
Don't invent intermediate spacing values or text opacities.
Don't nest containers: no card in a row, no row in a card, never two cards deep.
Don't make a primary button Signal-colored, or use Signal decoratively.
Don't hard-wrap dynamic text with literal newlines; ellipsize.
Don't drift toward torrent-site UI, streaming-app art, or the SaaS dashboard cliché.
Don't cast a shadow on anything.
Don't use color as the only carrier of status meaning.
Don't reach for a modal beyond the add-torrent dialog.
Don't write persuasive or benefit-led copy.
